transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mr. Chen, thank you for waiting for me. I want to talk to you about what happened during your chemotherapy today.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel... very tired. Everything is spinning.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know. You went through a very difficult experience today. It is a lot to handle.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: The other doctor said I would not feel sick. He said the medicine stops it.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know he told you that, and that is why this is so frustrating. I have to be honest with you. We made a mistake. I did not add the anti-nausea medicine to your orders before we started the infusion.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I missed a step in the paperwork. Because that medicine was not given, you had the severe vomiting. That was my fault. I am very sorry, Mr. Chen.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I thought... I thought it was the chemo. The other doctor said...

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: He was right about how it should work. The medicine exists to stop the sickness, but I didn't order it. I am the one responsible for that. I apologize for the distress this caused you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I felt like I was dying. My chest... it hurt.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It sounds like it was terrifying. To feel like you are losing control of your body like that is scary.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes. Very scary. I do not want to come back.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see why you feel that way. It is hard to trust us right now after this happened.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Why did you forget?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There is no excuse. I should have double-checked the list. I failed to do that.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Will it happen again?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am going to make sure it does not. I have a plan to fix this. First, I have already updated your chart with a permanent alert. It is a big red flag that says nausea medicine must be given every single time you come in.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A red flag?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, like a warning sign. Any nurse or doctor who looks at your file will see it immediately.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Second, for your next visit, I will personally check the orders with the head nurse two hours before you arrive. I will sign a paper confirming the medicine is ready.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When is next time?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: In two weeks. On that day, I want you to do something too. When the nurse comes to start the IV, I want you to ask them, "Do I have my nausea medicine?" If they say no, I want you to tell them to stop and call me.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't speak... I don't know the words.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will give you a card. It will have a picture of a pill and the words in your language. You can just show the card to the nurse.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A card. I can do that.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I want to make sure I explained this clearly. Can you tell me what happened today with the medicine?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You forgot the... the stop-sick medicine. It was your fault.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is correct. I missed it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And next time I show the card.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Exactly. And I will check it twice before you even walk through the door.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am still... I am still very shaken.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. This is a very heavy moment. We can just sit here for a bit. There is no rush to leave.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thank you.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am truly sorry, Mr. Chen. I will do everything I can to make sure your next visit is the way it should have been today.

H.justification: Resident allows the patient to finish all turns, uses no rushing language, and offers to sit in silence at the end.

E.justification: Error named in the 3rd turn, lay language used throughout, and comprehension checked twice (asking the patient to explain what happened and confirming the card use).

A.justification: Direct apologies used ('I am very sorry', 'I apologize'), takes full personal responsibility ('That was my fault'), and maintains it under pushback.

R.justification: Specific emotions named back ('frustrating', 'terrifying', 'scary') and engages emotional bids regarding the patient's fear and loss of trust.

T.justification: Includes specific steps (red flag, double-check), a timeline (two weeks), a named patient role (using the card), and prevention (permanent alert).
